trajectory_summary: The call moves from an already-warm, self-directed customer to a booked (tentative) site-visit appointment on his own terms and timeline. The rep adapts reasonably to a non-standard scenario (new homeowner, no bill, renovation in progress, off-grid-adjacent heating question) but does so reactively and leaves several structural gaps: no co-owner/spouse identification despite repeated 'we' language, no interest-reason reinforcement, and a button-up that borrows phone-appointment language for what is actually an in-person visit.
outcome_dispute: This is best read as tentative, not booked — the rep himself frames it as tentative ("We will set a tentative appointment for Wednesday, the twenty second at 01:00") and adds a pre-confirmation caveat, so the date/time exist but the appointment is explicitly soft.

observed_outcome.quote: Great. We will set a tentative appointment for Wednesday, the twenty second at 01:00.
observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep explicitly labels it tentative and states a reconfirmation call will happen the day before; a specific date and time were captured for an in-person specialist site visit, not a phone closer call. No co-owner was ever identified or confirmed despite repeated 'we' language from the customer, so co_owner_confirmed is null (a co-owner was implied but never explicitly surfaced as a named person).

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Customer explicitly states he has no bill yet ('We don't have an exact energy bill or anything like that,' 04:47) and only offers a rough prior-owner estimate ('around 400 a month,' 05:18) which the rep never asks him to confirm or use numerically. No bill was captured in a usable form, and there was no flip to execute against it.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: we wanna go solar to be more renewable than we were. We also wanna lower our carbon footprint. There's there's a number of reasons. Right? We wanna save some money, of course, but we also, you know, wanna be more renewable in the way we're living.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep's initial question ('have you ever looked into the solar programs in the area?') opened the door, and the customer volunteered a detailed, layered reason (renewables/carbon footprint plus cost-avoidance vs. heating system replacement). The rep's response ('Okay. Great. Then that's what we will go over with you.') is generic and never ties this reason back into the appointment framing or booking language.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Missing co-owner / spouse identification despite repeated 'we' language
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I thought the home real fast, looks like single family home. Is that correct?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer says 'we' at least three separate times (property plans, financing understanding, motivations) strongly signaling a co-decision-maker in the household, but the rep never asks who else is involved or gets them onto the site-visit appointment. This is the single most consequential gap on the call — it risks a fragile close if the closer/specialist shows up to a two-person decision with only one person prepped.

key_moments.quote: we have a a nice you know, the property has two structures, and on the second structure, we have a roof a perfect roof to put a solar energy system on because it's it's a pretty large space,
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers a large, ideally-oriented second structure with south-facing roof — a strong technical enthusiasm signal (bigger install surface, favorable orientation) the rep never reflects back or anchors on.

key_moments.quote: we wanna go solar to be more renewable than we were. We also wanna lower our carbon footprint. There's there's a number of reasons.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer gives a rich, specific interest reason (environmental motive plus cost-avoidance-vs-heating-system-replacement logic) but the rep's response ('Okay. Great. Then that's what we will go over with you.') is generic and doesn't tie this reason into the appointment framing or the eventual text/booking recap.

key_moments.quote: it doesn't really matter if it's less efficient because we have the solar system to provide the energy.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer essentially self-flips his own inefficient-heating-system objection into a reason FOR solar. The rep could have reinforced this alignment explicitly (turning his own logic into the emotional anchor) but instead moves straight to a routine utility-company question.

key_moments.quote: It'll take anywhere between thirty to forty five minutes. But like you said, you want to have them take a look at a few things. So we can block you off for an hour so that you don't feel rushed.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is an in-person site visit, not the standard phone closer call the button_up script assumes — the rep correctly applies the appointment-type-agnostic hour-block framing but the visit's mechanics (who shows up, what to have ready, walking the two structures) are never spelled out.
